modules.summary: `xml.document` — a small read-only tree built from `XmlReader` events.
modules.description:
API responses are small and are read by *path*: "every
`reservationSet/item/instancesSet/item`, and under each its `instanceType`".
That is awkward over a pull parser and natural over a tree, so `Document`
builds one — but flat, as parallel arrays indexed by node id, rather than as
recursive structs. A node is an element; its text is the concatenation of
its direct text children (whitespace-only runs between child elements are
dropped), which is the only text model an API response needs.

```mojo
var doc = Document.parse(body)
for item in doc.find_all(doc.root(), "reservationSet/item/instancesSet/item"):
    print(doc.child_text(item, "instanceId"), doc.find_text(item, "instanceState/name"))
```

Path segments match the *local* name, so a namespace prefix on the document
side never has to be spelled out. `*` matches any element.

modules.summary: `xml.reader` — a pull parser over an in-memory XML document.
modules.description:
`XmlReader.next()` hands back one `XmlEvent` at a time: a start tag (with its
attributes), an end tag, a run of text, or end of input. Self-closing tags
produce a start *and* an end event, so a consumer never has to special-case
`<a/>`. Comments, processing instructions, the XML declaration and DOCTYPE are
skipped; CDATA sections come back as text, verbatim.

Entity references are decoded in text and attribute values: the five
predefined ones (`<` `>` `&` `"` `'`) and numeric
character references (`A`, `A`). Anything else is an error rather
than being passed through, because an API response carrying an undeclared
entity is malformed and silently keeping `&foo;` would hide that.

What this is not: a validating parser. It checks that tags nest and close
with matching names — the property every consumer relies on — and nothing
about DTDs or schemas. Namespaces are left as written (`ec2:item` stays
`ec2:item`); `local_name` strips a prefix when a consumer wants to ignore it.

structs.summary: Pull parser over a document held in memory.
structs.description:
The reader owns a copy of the bytes, so the source string may go away.
Call `next()` until it returns an `EVENT_EOF` event; a malformed document
raises with the byte offset where parsing stopped.

overloads.summary: How many elements are open at the current position.
True when `s` is only XML whitespace — the indentation between tags.
`ec2:item` → `item`; a name without a prefix is returned unchanged.
